source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition

coverage.scope: E. serial filing abuse, §109(g) 180-day bar, §§362(c)(3),(4) and 362(b)(21) multiple filings, §521(i) 45/46-day incomplete paperwork, §362(d)(4) in rem property relief, §§362(b)(20),(22),(23),(l),(m) and eviction, integrated exam workflow
coverage.notice: Source dates and wording are historical casebook treatment. Notes preserve source rather than independently certifying postpublication changes.

topics.title: E. Serial Bankruptcy Filings: §109(g) and Stay-Limiting Refiling Provisions
topics.description: Stopping repeated skeletal petitions used to interrupt foreclosures and evictions.

entries.title: Why broad self-executing automatic stay invites face-sheet filing abuse
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Filing skeletal §301 petition can trigger stay without elaborate motion; debtor may omit schedules, allow dismissal, then file again on next foreclosure date, using stay as delay tool not legitimate bankruptcy debt adjustment.
entries.laymanExplanation: Someone repeatedly files enough papers to freeze house auction and then does nothing to resolve debt.
entries.legalExplanation: Source describes commercial abuses targeting distressed owners/tenants; creditor needs mechanisms to stop repetitive interruptions.
entries.examApplication: In hypothetical identify sequence of filings, dismissals, lack of schedules and goal of delaying a specific lender.
entries.examTrap: Do not treat every second bankruptcy as automatically fraudulent; statute defines triggers.

entries.title: §109(g)(1): 180-day debtor eligibility bar for willful noncompliance
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: An individual whose previous case was dismissed for willful failure to obey court orders or appear in proper prosecution within preceding 180 days is ineligible to file new bankruptcy.
entries.laymanExplanation: Miss hearings on purpose, court dismisses, then can't immediately file again.
entries.legalExplanation: Requires statutory misconduct trigger and time measurement, not any ordinary dismissal.
entries.examApplication: Check dismissal grounds, willfulness, date of new petition.
entries.examTrap: Not every procedural mistake or every dismissal qualifies under (g)(1).

entries.title: §109(g)(2): voluntary dismissal after stay-relief motion
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Chapter13 debtor voluntarily dismissing AFTER creditor files motion for stay relief may trigger 180-day ineligibility under §109(g)(2).
entries.laymanExplanation: Can't reliably avoid penalty by quitting before judge decides lender's stay motion.
entries.legalExplanation: Requires relation of pending stay relief request and voluntary dismissal as source describes.
entries.examApplication: Build timeline lender motion → debtor voluntary dismissal → next filing.
entries.examTrap: Don't conflate court-dismissed willful nonappearance with voluntary-dismissal branch.

entries.title: §362(b)(21): new petitions violating refiling prohibition no stay
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: §362(b)(21)(A) excepts cases filed in violation of §109(g) 180-day eligibility bar; (B) excepts filing contrary to court order prohibiting another filing.
entries.laymanExplanation: Invalid repeat filing can't automatically pause foreclosure again.
entries.legalExplanation: Works with §109(g) and broader judicial refiling injunction.
entries.examApplication: Identify prior order and its terms as well as any 180-day clock.
entries.examTrap: Don't assume unrelated debtor's new eligible filing necessarily invalid under §109(g).

entries.title: §362(c)(3): one case dismissed in prior year, 30-day stay termination
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: For individual Chapter7/11/13 with previous case dismissed within year (excluding specified §707(b) scenario), subsequent automatic stay described as terminating after day30 absent successful timely request proving good faith.
entries.laymanExplanation: After one recent failed case, protection may run out after a month unless debtor justifies new filing.
entries.legalExplanation: Presumptions of bad faith in §362(c)(3)(C) may demand clear and convincing rebuttal, statutory details important.
entries.examApplication: Distinguish initial stay in place with impending expiration vs no stay at all.
entries.examTrap: Source's shorthand does not resolve all later judicial interpretation disputes about scope of §362(c)(3).

entries.title: §362(c)(4): two or more recent dismissals, no initial stay
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Where two prior individual bankruptcy cases dismissed within preceding year, later filing generally has NO automatic stay on filing; debtor can seek order imposing stay via prompt request within 30 days and affirmative good faith showing.
entries.laymanExplanation: After repeated recent cases, bankruptcy filing no longer freezes foreclosure immediately.
entries.legalExplanation: §362(c)(4)(D) bad-faith presumption and clear-and-convincing rebuttal may apply.
entries.examApplication: Compare one prior dismissal (stay begins then lapses) to two (stay doesn't begin).
entries.examTrap: Don't say §362(c)(3) and (c)(4) have identical default results.

entries.title: Bad-faith presumption and clear convincing proof
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Statutes §§362(c)(3)(C),(c)(4)(D) specify circumstances presuming new filing not in good faith, rebuttable only by clear and convincing evidence.
entries.laymanExplanation: Debtor may need solid proof new case truly aimed at viable debt resolution.
entries.legalExplanation: Discuss missed prior plan, changed finances or real new prospect as fact-based rebuttal evidence (examples are analysis, not stipulated facts).
entries.examApplication: Ask why earlier cases failed and what changed.
entries.examTrap: No universal presumption covering every single second filing under all circumstances.

entries.title: §521(i): incomplete individual petitions may automatically dismiss day46
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Source describes failure to file §521(a)(1) required schedules/statements/certificates within 45 days leading to automatic dismissal on 46th; debtor may request up to 45 more days for sufficient justification; trustee may invoke creditor-benefit/good-faith payment-evidence exception; court confirms dismissal upon request.
entries.laymanExplanation: Handing in cover page isn't enough to keep case forever without financial documents.
entries.legalExplanation: The two exceptions and court order confirmation under §521(i)(2) are separate timelines.
entries.examApplication: For repeated face-sheet pattern note 45-day document clock and statutory possible extensions/waiver.
entries.examTrap: Automatic dismissal provisions have procedural nuances; don't claim no judicial action can ever affect them.

entries.title: Clock comparison: 180 days, one year, 30 days and 45/46
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: §109(g) 180-day eligibility; §362(c)(3)/(4) look back one year and provide 30-day stay continuation/imposition request; §521(i) documents by day45/dismissal day46, subject exceptions.
entries.laymanExplanation: Four different clocks solve four different problems: eligibility, prior cases, stay duration, missing paperwork.
entries.legalExplanation: Memorize statute and starting event for each; don't swap clocks.
entries.examApplication: Write deadline timeline rather than memorizing number without trigger.
entries.examTrap: Not a single universal '30-day bankruptcy deadline'.

topics.title: E. §362(d)(4) In Rem Stay Relief: Property-Specific Foreclosure Protection
topics.description: Fractional interest transfers and recorded two-year orders binding later bankruptcy filers.

entries.title: Fractional-interest transfers exploit person-specific stay
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Property owner facing foreclosure transfers tiny fractional real estate interests to multiple nominal holders; separate holder files a bankruptcy in succession to make 100% sale impossible, evading limits on original debtor's refiling.
entries.laymanExplanation: People rotate tiny ownership percentages into new bankruptcy petitions so auction keeps being blocked.
entries.legalExplanation: Source explains why §109(g) and §362(c) person-based serial rules are insufficient.
entries.examApplication: Identify deed transfer dates, multiple different debtors and same target property.
entries.examTrap: Don't mistake ordinary coownership alone for fraudulent scheme; intent and statutory predicates matter.

entries.title: §362(d)(4): realty scheme to delay, hinder and defraud (source wording)
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Textbook edition describes court authority to grant real-property stay relief for petition as part of scheme to delay/hinder/defraud involving (A) transfer of any interest without secured creditor consent or (B) multiple bankruptcy filings affecting real property.
entries.laymanExplanation: Judge can stop rotating filings from freezing the SAME house.
entries.legalExplanation: Source's phrasing is its historical statutory wording; use quote of assigned source when studying, do not silently update text.
entries.examApplication: Test scheme evidence and one of transfer/multiple filing alternatives.
entries.examTrap: No automatic (d)(4) remedy just because someone filed once and owes mortgage.

entries.title: Recorded in rem order binds later cases involving same property for two years
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: If §362(d)(4) order recorded in public real-property interest/lien records, it binds other bankruptcy cases purporting to affect the same property filed within two years; §362(b)(20) provides corresponding exception.
entries.laymanExplanation: Even if a new coowner files, the recorded order follows real estate for two years.
entries.legalExplanation: Grounded on property, not just debtor identity; ensures foreclosure can proceed despite rotating filers.
entries.examApplication: Include recordation and 2-year clock in answer.
entries.examTrap: Without proper recordation, do not assume statutory two-year effect automatically applies.

entries.title: Subsequent debtor may seek relief from in rem order
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Later debtor can request relief from recorded order for changed circumstances or good cause after notice and hearing; until then bankruptcy filing does not stay lien enforcement on that land under §362(b)(20).
entries.laymanExplanation: A genuine new owner may ask court to reconsider if situation materially changed.
entries.legalExplanation: Safeguards legitimate parties against overbroad lasting order.
entries.examApplication: Identify new financial/property facts and formal request.
entries.examTrap: A recorded order isn't necessarily unchallengeable for two years.

entries.title: Comparison: personal refiling versus property-specific in rem
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: §109(g) and §362(c)(3)/(4) target individual's repeated cases; §362(d)(4) and §362(b)(20) target repeat filings by ANY individual affecting same real property through recorded order.
entries.laymanExplanation: If borrowers rotate, property-focused order succeeds where person-focused bar fails.
entries.legalExplanation: This is critical conceptual contrast in casebook questions.
entries.examApplication: Use separate columns: whose conduct, trigger, effect and duration.
entries.examTrap: Do not confuse §362(d)(4) in rem relief with §362(c)(4) no stay after two personal dismissals.

topics.title: E. Residential Eviction Exceptions: Possession Judgment, Cure and Danger

entries.title: §362(b)(22): prepetition residential possession judgment exception
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Under 2005 amendment, lessor with state-law judgment for possession of residential tenancy entered BEFORE bankruptcy may proceed with eviction despite normally broad stay, subject statutory §362(l) temporary cure process.
entries.laymanExplanation: Landlord already won possession before bankruptcy; tenant's filing may not stop eviction.
entries.legalExplanation: Recognizes residual possessory interest could otherwise trigger stay despite eviction judgment.
entries.examApplication: Identify judgment entry relative petition; don't equate mere late rent with possession judgment.
entries.examTrap: Judgment required for this particular exception, not merely landlord notice.

entries.title: §362(l): limited 30-day cure route for residential tenant
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: When applicable nonbankruptcy law permits curing basis for possession judgment, tenant may file timely certification with petition to obtain limited 30-day stay and must effect cure and certify within that period to preserve stated protection.
entries.laymanExplanation: Tenant may get 30 days to fix unpaid-rent problem if state law allows that.
entries.legalExplanation: Very specific petition-time certificate and cure requirements; state cure rights matter.
entries.examApplication: Compare case where law permits paying rent to undo judgment vs final noncurable possession.
entries.examTrap: Not universal 30-day extension without certifications or legal cure right.

entries.title: §362(b)(23), §362(m): dangerous property or drug-related use
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Special expedited landlord process when eviction grounded in endangerment of rental property or illegal controlled substance use at premises, as described by §362(b)(23) and implemented by §362(m).
entries.laymanExplanation: Dangerous tenant activity gets different protection than ordinary overdue rent.
entries.legalExplanation: Understand separate from judgment-for-possession exception and required lessor certification/procedures.
entries.examApplication: When facts mention property danger or illegal drug use, flag separate path.
entries.examTrap: Do not assume all eviction claims are identical or automatically stayed.

entries.title: Why residential possessory interest matters despite judgment
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Before explicit §362(b)(22), debtor's residual rights of possession under lease and state eviction law could be regarded as estate property or acts against debtor, potentially staying enforcement; Congress crafted targeted exception.
entries.laymanExplanation: Even an eviction judgment may leave tenant holding an interest that automatic stay would protect without special exception.
entries.legalExplanation: Book poses exact why-statute-needed question; avoid overclaiming state rights identical in every jurisdiction.
entries.examApplication: Discuss why initial automatic stay might otherwise apply despite judgment.
entries.examTrap: The exception isn't proof debtor has no property interest whatsoever.

topics.title: Chapter 7 Master Exam Map: Which Stay-Relief Ground, Which Clock, Which Remedy?
topics.description: Integrated algorithm and arithmetic checklists for final exam issue spotting.

entries.title: Step 1: identify chapter, asset and stay duration
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Determine what act is stayed, against estate or debtor, bankruptcy chapter and whether §362(c) already ended protection. Assess any serial-filer or eviction exception before asking for discretionary relief.
entries.laymanExplanation: Don't litigate stay relief if no stay actually in effect.
entries.legalExplanation: Check §362(c), (b)(20)-(23), §109(g) and filing history first.
entries.examApplication: Mark filing, dismissal, prior cases, debt nature, court judgments.
entries.examTrap: Automatic stay is broad but not immortal.

entries.title: Step 2: independent §362(d)(1) adequacy and §362(d)(2) equity/plan tests
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: If stay remains: cause under (d)(1), especially actual lien-value decline unprotected; separately (d)(2) creditor proves no debtor equity, opposing party shows asset needed for realistically successful reorganization.
entries.laymanExplanation: Ask two questions: bank harmed? Is property genuinely needed for viable bankruptcy?
entries.legalExplanation: Alyucan/Timbers limit protections and Pegasus requires verifiable feasibility.
entries.examApplication: Show which side bears proof for EACH issue.
entries.examTrap: No equity and lack of AP are not same statutory requirement.

entries.title: Step 3: choose §361 remedy then fallback §507(b)
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: If threatened decline, use cash depreciation coverage, new lien, indubitable equivalent; if initial protection later fails consider §507(b) superpriority. Interest-based opportunity cost alone excluded for undersecured by Timbers.
entries.laymanExplanation: Protect lender against property losing value, not merely waiting to foreclose.
entries.legalExplanation: §361(3) does not permit simply granting admin expense initially; later §507(b) distinct.
entries.examApplication: For Problems 7.1–7.2 separate collateral loss, expected payment and actual result.
entries.examTrap: Don't automatically substitute contractual interest for AP payment.

entries.title: Step 4: check §552 cash collateral and special SARE interest
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Prepetition lien on proceeds or rents may attach postpetition under §552(b) when applicable rights perfected, despite §552(a) default; §363 regulates cash use. If SARE §101(51B), debtor timely files feasible plan OR pays secured-value monthly nondefault interest under (d)(3).
entries.laymanExplanation: Is money actually bank's collateral? And does property qualify as passive real estate?
entries.legalExplanation: Problem7.4 old/new contracts; 7.5 rents; 7.6 SARE and rent overlap.
entries.examApplication: Compute separate secured interest, rent gross/net and SARE rate.
entries.examTrap: Do not give bank every postpetition paycheck based on prefiling blanket lien.

entries.title: Step 5: fast procedures, terms and renewals
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Under §362(e), §362(f) emergency and 2005 individual-specific deadline, choose hearing pace, potential conditioning vs termination; early stay relief denial doesn't bar later motion when plan prospects decline.
entries.laymanExplanation: Judge can say 'keep property if debtor pays and files plan in 60 days' rather than binary keep/end.
entries.legalExplanation: Time clocks vary; distinguish §362(d)(4) property orders from (c)(4) repeated-person filing.
entries.examApplication: Write both clock and event that starts it.
entries.examTrap: A court denying motion once hasn't conclusively blessed debtor's plan forever.

entries.title: Numeric calculator 1: debtor equity under §362(d)(2)(A)
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Equity of debtor in property = debtor's legally valued property interest − sum of all secured liens, using evidence and applicable proposed use/disposition. If ≤0, no residual equity; creditor proves this fact.
entries.laymanExplanation: Only the money after ALL mortgages is debtor equity.
entries.legalExplanation: Loan-to-value percentage of ONE lien is not debtor's total equity.
entries.examApplication: Use for Problem7.3; keep result unsolved.
entries.examTrap: Do not subtract first mortgage alone while ignoring second.

entries.title: Numeric calculator 2: depreciation cushion and §507(b) shortfall framework
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Projected AP need per month corresponds to loss in secured interest from depreciation (subject protected-value limits). Cushion horizon = cushion÷(monthly collateral decline+relevant debt increase). For failed AP, quantify actual protected-interest decline and compare value already given via ordered protection, then analyze §507(b) entitlement.
entries.laymanExplanation: A $50k margin eroding $3k per month lasts about 16.7 months; actual unexpected loss may need statutory remedy.
entries.legalExplanation: Avoid double counting already paid cash and property sale proceeds against underlying claim.
entries.examApplication: Apply framework to 7.1 & 7.2, not answers.
entries.examTrap: Do not treat any negative margin as automatic superpriority without statutory prerequisites.

entries.title: Numeric calculator 3: SARE interest, principal selection
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Monthly interest obligation when §362(d)(3)(B) applies can be framed as nondefault contract annual rate × value of allowed SECURED claim ÷12, distinct from lender's larger total loan and total property rents.
entries.laymanExplanation: Pay interest on lien collateral value, not fictitious fully secured $25m when property supports less.
entries.legalExplanation: Source Problem7.6 gives both $125k whole-debt interest and $100k secured interest to test correct statutory base.
entries.examApplication: Place gross rents, net collateral rents, secured claim and total debt on separate lines.
entries.examTrap: Do not mistake rent available to pay interest for required interest principal.

entries.title: Case selection one-line map
entries.source: User-provided Bankruptcy casebook Chapter 7 §E The Automatic Stay and Abusive Serial Filings, plus chapter-wide structured exam maps; statutes as described in assigned source-era edition
entries.summary: Alyucan: no mandated preservation of interest-eroding cushion with stable realty; Timbers: undersecured no lost foreclosure opportunity AP; Pegasus: reject speculative reorganization feasibility; Larry Goodwin Golf: active golf services outside passive SARE.
entries.laymanExplanation: Each opinion matches a different legal inquiry: cushion, delay, real plan, property classification.
entries.legalExplanation: When asked case analogy lead with issue and section, not just case name.
entries.examApplication: In exam, apply cases to statute §361, §362(d)(1), (d)(2), (d)(3) in that order.
entries.examTrap: Don't cite golf course classification as if deciding Timbers opportunity cost.
